name: Hezekiah
overview: Hezekiah was a male king of Judah, the son of Ahaz, who trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. His reign is noted for his reliance on God during times of crisis and his leadership in spiritual reform within Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Hezekiah means 'y-h-v-h is [my] strength,' reflecting a personal trust in God. He is also referred to by the titles King Hezekiah and King of Judah, which emphasize his royal authority over the southern kingdom.
familyAndRelationships: Hezekiah was the son of Ahaz and the father of Abi. It is also inferred that Manasseh was his son. These relationships place Hezekiah within the Davidic royal lineage, important for the continuity of Judah's monarchy.
scriptureSignificance: Hezekiah is significant in Scripture as a righteous king who removed idolatry and restored proper worship of God in Judah. His trust in the LORD is highlighted during the Assyrian threat when his prayers led to God's deliverance of Jerusalem. Additionally, God extended his life by fifteen years after a serious illness, underscoring divine favor on his faithful leadership.
